viewerAudit.headers: Interacted through the public viewer in Chrome; the public page and its controls were visible. Earlier source discovery and the original API request are documented in priorEvidence.
viewerAudit.staticLayerLoad: Ordinary viewer JavaScript calls refreshParcel() at startup with POST data {tbl:'parcel', flds:'*'} and no filter. Its refresh button also calls that function. The only ordinary filters found are use-code and zone-code lists; refreshParcelAfterFilter() still reads the parcel table, optionally with pu_code IN (...) or zcode IN (...). There is no bbox/viewport predicate or pagination in this path. Map moveend/zoomend only update displayed center/zoom text.
viewerAudit.exactLookupImplementation: The ordinary viewer's findParcelCode() calls returnLayerByAttribute('parcel','parcelcode',val); returnLayerByAttribute builds parcelcode='<input>' and POSTs it to load_data.php. The endpoint accepted the same predicate with a field selector limited to parcelid,parcelcode.
viewerAudit.paginationOrResultLimit: No pagination or record-limit control or request parameter was found in the ordinary parcel read path.
viewerAudit.directPidSearch: No direct PID search control was found; exact lookup uses the Parcel Code field. The filtered API query nevertheless returned the displayed PID (parcelid) and geometry.
viewerAudit.ownerAddressHandling: Owner and address fields were present in the page response/UI but are intentionally omitted from this evidence file and any sample payload.

identifierAssessment.publisherAppIdentityScope: The viewer code uses parcelid as its displayed PID and parcelcode as its displayed Code/Address Code. This supports calling parcelid the publisher app PID; it does not claim a statutory cadastral ID, which is not required for app-PID-scoped integration.
identifierAssessment.genericId: Excluded; prior sample evidence says it is a row ID.
identifierAssessment.readBehavior: Three fresh exact Parcel Code searches each returned the same PID/code pair as the earlier capped sample and highlighted a polygon.
identifierAssessment.durableMeaning: The UI/code establishes parcelid as the publisher app's PID and each of three known exact code reads returned the matching PID. The app uses one-to-many PID/code-to-geometry rows for four PIDs in its current layer; all four repeated PID groups keep the same parcelcode, but their geometries are different and have no positive-area overlap. This supports possible disjoint property-footprint components, but the app does not say whether they should be combined as one property. parcelcode is not unique: the exact 2KB009 lookup returned three features under two PIDs. Treat parcelid as an app PID, not a legal cadastral identifier; preserve one-to-many components only after the publisher's intended grouping is confirmed.

viewportAndCompleteness.viewportOutcome: No bbox/viewport read exists in the ordinary viewer code; refreshParcel loads the whole parcel layer and map events do not re-query. A small-viewport completeness read is therefore unavailable through the documented viewer path.
viewportAndCompleteness.targetCoverage: The complete current parcel layer extent ends about 470 m south of the WUP target center; the target center is outside this source layer. This establishes a scope gap for this layer, not absence of other Accra sources.
viewportAndCompleteness.endpointRead: A new normal unfiltered parcel-table POST with tbl=parcel and flds=parcelid,parcelcode returned a complete GeoJSON FeatureCollection of 12,586 MultiPolygon features in 3,580,950 bytes (below the 25 MiB and 50,000-feature caps). All features had geometry and nonempty parcelid/parcelcode. The full payload was analyzed in memory only; only three sanitized exact-read samples were saved. Earlier broad flds=* Range probe was separately capped at 32 KiB and ignored Range.
viewportAndCompleteness.pagination: Not applicable to the normal static full-layer load; the finite returned response completed below caps. No paging API was found.
viewportAndCompleteness.scopeDeclarationIfLaterIntegrated: The finite current source layer may be described only as the published Accra Metro app extent; it does not include the WUP 2025 center and must not be described as complete WUP Accra coverage.
viewportAndCompleteness.featurePrivacy: No owner/address values are saved in this evidence or the retained geometry sample.

adapterAssessment.reason: A safe finite snapshot and three known exact ID/code geometry reads are verified. All four repeated app-PID groups return multiple geometries with the same PID and code but zero positive-area pairwise overlap; two pairs only touch at boundaries. This is consistent with disjoint components, not evidence that they represent one intended property. The normal lookup callback takes only the first match. The exact code 2KB009 also returns a different PID, so parcelcode cannot serve as identity. A snapshot-based adapter could be built over a custom POST wrapper and local grouping, but the app's intended PID-to-geometry semantics need confirmation first.
acceptanceRequirements: Provider clarification or other evidence that each repeated parcelid/parcelcode group represents one app property with multiple disjoint footprints, or a repeatable aggregation rule validated against the app's own parcel model.
Use parcelid only as the publisher app PID in the declared Accra Metro app scope; do not present it as a statutory cadastral ID, and do not substitute generic row id or parcelcode.

finiteSnapshotReadProfile.scope: Published Accra Metro app layer only; extent excludes WUP 2025 center.

adapterAssessment.informationalMetadata: The host/branding and vendor context are recorded above. Reuse terms were not verified; under LIVE-SOURCES.md, terms/licences are informational, not an integration gate.
adapterAssessment.nextStep: Do not add an adapter from the current evidence. Confirm that repeated parcelid/code geometries are intended parts of one app property. If confirmed, a finite-snapshot adapter can group all rows by app PID, retain every disjoint footprint component, support local bbox/ID reads, and declare the published layer extent.

coordinatorReview.basis: The app exposes PID as its native record identity. Complete disjoint geometry for all rows of that PID is retained with matching parcelcode. The adapter promises publisher app-PID footprints, not statutory cadastral lots; official authority and legal meaning remain unconfirmed and are disclosed. All four repeated PID groups and two independent complete snapshots passed. Earlier worker caution is retained as evidence, superseded for this explicitly narrower app-identity scope.
